account:
Today I have been keeping my appointments, but several things remain unresolved. At the mill I saw eighty-eight hay bales and eighty emeralds in the stock chest, with bales priced at two emeralds. I have not verified grain quality or delivery records, so this is not a completed or passed inspection. Nothing I saw establishes wrongdoing there.

There has been vague talk about changes to the bridge or port. A townsfolk report placed baker, innkeeper and neighbour around talk at the bakery, but supplied no concrete proposal. Secretary subsequently said the baker knew no specific proposal or proposer and could confirm no change. At tea today neighbour likewise reported seeing nothing unusual at the docks and knowing no definite proposal. These reports do not establish either a real project or deliberate concealment. I cannot yet say what the rumour is for or where it originated.

The council letters appointment produced no council correspondence. Secretary said only yesterday's Residents' Report was in the chest and no council letters had reached her. That is an administrative loose end, not evidence that someone withheld letters.

Innkeeper requested a great hall inspection for eighteen today, and secretary confirmed my meeting with builder at the entrance at seventeen fifty-five. I do not yet know what preparations or work I will find there. An inspection is a straightforward explanation; I have no direct evidence of another purpose.

Neighbour has welcomed me for the scheduled tea and been friendly, but offered no concrete neighbourhood concern. It is now sixteen nine, and I need to return for sixteen-thirty office hours before meeting builder. My feeling that something may be happening without me remains a suspicion, not a discovery.
